notes: A customer with no enabled Conditional Access policy and no security defaults sees one finding for it, with the five gaps that follow listed under it, instead of six findings for one fact. A customer on security defaults is no longer told that legacy authentication is open or that administrators lack MFA. Install the Backend update released with this one, or the findings keep their old shape.
The saved named locations of a backup stay on screen while the panel reads them again, and Retry clears an earlier error before it tries.

A customer with no enabled Conditional Access policy and no security defaults sees one finding for it, with the five gaps that follow listed under it, instead of six findings for one fact. A customer on security defaults is no longer told that legacy authentication is open or that administrators lack MFA. Install the Backend update released with this one, or the findings keep their old shape.
The saved named locations of a backup stay on screen while the panel reads them again, and Retry clears an earlier error before it tries.

A customer's own pages now count an Azure finding once per check, the way every other page already did: a check that fires in two subscriptions is one finding, and the rows per subscription stay as the list under it. The theme page says how many subscriptions its number spans.
The customer setup wizard names its service checkboxes, Azure coverage choices and email field for every screen reader.

Invitations you prepare show as pending on the Customers page, with the progress of each service, until the customer approves or you dismiss them. The mail-app link opens a short message with the approval links, and the designed download is the full invitation.

The Dashboard and the Customers page count findings the same way, connection meters read approved Azure access as connected, and invoice lines are named by plan in English. Install the Backend update released with this one, or pending invitations, invoice names and the renewal date after a purchase stay missing.

An approval given in a different organisation is refused with a page that says so. The Remove dialog says what removal does and leaves alone, every entry point says Add customer, and the setup wizard's controls are named for assistive technology.

The AI writer is gone. Findings and opportunities show their written description only, the AI writer tab is removed from Settings, and the update notice lists the Portal and the Backend. Install the Backend update released with this one.
The portal uses no AI service, inside or outside your deployment, and nothing from your customers' tenants is sent to one.

Before a purchase, the plan page shows the email address Checkout will use and lets you change it, so receipts go to the right place. Install the Backend update released with this one: without it the change is refused.
The plan page no longer mentions a free first month. No trial is offered: the amount shown is charged when you subscribe, and the 30-day money-back guarantee runs from that first payment.

Findings over time starts where your records start. A customer connected an hour ago shows one hour of history, and the moments before it are marked as no snapshot, instead of a flat day that never happened. Install the Backend update released with this one: with the older Backend the chart still repeats the first reading across the whole day.
The invitation wizard says, next to the administrator's email, that whoever opens the approval link connects their own tenant, so the invitation must go to an administrator in the customer's tenant.
The plan offers carry the guarantee from the terms: cancel at any time, and within 30 days of your first payment you can ask for that payment back in full.
The page shown after a payment speaks to a first buyer: every customer you connect streams from the moment it approves, and its button takes you to connect or view customers.
The banner on an empty portfolio says what to do next, connect your first customer, and leaves pricing to the plan page.

A customer invitation is prepared in the portal and sent from your own mail program. Open in your mail app fills in the message, and Download gives the designed email. Send through Basewiser is offered only when email delivery is set up on your backend.

Wherever the portal points you to Basewiser for help, such as the help window, error pages and the update notice, the address is support@basewiser.com. Sales and general questions stay with contact@basewiser.com.
This update and the Backend update can be installed in either order.
Line charts no longer stretch into tall blocks when they sit beside a taller card. They keep a height that suits their width and stay at the bottom of the card.
Large line charts use a light fill that fades out, so the line stays easy to read. In stacked charts each band is filled only down to the band below it, so the colours no longer overlap and mix.
On a Case, the time it was opened is written the same way as the other times on the card.

When the Portal installs a Backend update, it also gives the Backend the Portal's own sign-in identity, which the Backend uses to recognise requests from the Portal. This update and the Backend update can be installed in either order.
Customer documents carry the Basewiser wordmark at the head of the cover, with the provider who prepared them named beneath. The wordmark matches the dark or light version of the document.

The Backups over time chart shows the number of backups each day on a whole-number scale, so a day with a backup is a full bar. The policy count is shown in the Latest backup panel beside the chart instead of as a line on it.
The controls at the top of each customer page sit on one row, and the Refresh button shows when the data was last synced. In a customer's menu, Opportunities is above Reports, as in the main menu.

Customer documents have a new design that leads with the figures that matter most, such as the price and the open findings. They report open findings per area instead of a 0 to 100 score, and every printed page carries the provider's name and a page number.
Assessments and proposals can be printed in NOK, SEK, DKK, EUR, USD or GBP. Amounts are converted at fixed rates, and the document states the rate it used.
The opportunity page shows how a project's price is built from its hours, the findings behind it by severity, and the customer's other open and delivered work.
The By severity ring in the Inbox now shows only the number of active cases, so no text runs into the ring.
A case opens with three answers: what happened, what it means and what to do next. The evidence follows in numbered sections, in the same layout for every kind of case.

With the matching Backend release, cases show where a change was made from: the IP address, the city and country, and whether the account used MFA. Role grants and exclusions also show whether the affected account is a member or a guest, whether it is enabled, its sign-in methods and its last sign-in.

Help and Feedback open in one window, and screenshots can be pasted into feedback. Toggles and tabs look and move the same on every page, status tags have no frame, and the Azure summary shows findings by severity and category.
Severity is shown as a coloured square and a word, without a frame, in tables, lists, notifications and reports. Reds, greens and ambers come from one consistent set.

Conditional Access drift marks each change by direction: green for added or turned on, red for removed or turned off, and amber for a value replaced by another. An open finding stands apart from the findings around it.
The update notice and the What's new overlay are redesigned. Display preferences, toggles and switches share one design, and text is no longer separated with centred dots.
Text across the portal is rewritten in plain, consistent wording, including messages, errors and empty states.
Opportunity summaries read as full sentences.
Finding, Alert and Case wording changes with the matching Backend release. The two updates can be installed in either order.

A tenant with no enabled Conditional Access policy and no security defaults gets one critical finding, with legacy authentication, MFA for administrators, risk-based access, sign-in location and device requirements listed under it. Each reports on its own again as soon as a first policy is enforced or security defaults are turned on.

Security defaults now satisfy the legacy authentication and administrator MFA checks. A finding folded into the one above closes as superseded, never as fixed, so a customer's history stays honest. Install the Portal update released with this one.

A tenant with no enabled Conditional Access policy and no security defaults gets one critical finding, with legacy authentication, MFA for administrators, risk-based access, sign-in location and device requirements listed under it. Each reports on its own again as soon as a first policy is enforced or security defaults are turned on.

Security defaults now satisfy the legacy authentication and administrator MFA checks. A finding folded into the one above closes as superseded, never as fixed, so a customer's history stays honest. Install the Portal update released with this one.

A new customer gets its first identity scan when it connects and its first Azure sweep within minutes, instead of waiting for the nightly runs. A first backup that did not land at connect is taken by the backup scheduler within a quarter of an hour.

The findings chart follows a removal, a first scan and a purchase at once, a purchase writes its renewal date, and invoice lines carry the plan behind them. Install this before the Portal update released with it.

Every refused registration is logged with its reason and attempt, the portal address becomes the customer's own domain at install, and the consent link carries the invited tenant so an approval in another organisation is refused.

The AI writer is removed: no drafts are written, stored or queued any more, and the two tables it used are no longer created. Install this with the Portal update released at the same time. A deployment that had the writer on keeps its job resource until it is deleted by hand, and that job never runs again.
The billing email on file can be changed from the portal before a purchase, so receipts and payment reminders go to the right address. Install this with the Portal update released at the same time.

Findings history is recorded from the first reading on and never filled in before it. A series is shorter than the day or week it is shown in until the history covers it, and a moment without a reading repeats the last one. Install this with the Portal update released at the same time: with the older Portal the chart's time labels can be off until both are in.

Setting up the Basewiser app no longer fails with a Microsoft Graph error when Entra needs a few seconds before a new app registration can receive its secret. The backend waits and retries, as it already did for the other form of the same delay.
The personal invitation and other messages that point to Basewiser for help name support@basewiser.com.
Break-glass declarations are recorded under the operator who is signed in. This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.

The Backend accepts the name of the signed-in Operator only from the Portal itself. A request that names an Operator without signing in is refused, and anyone who signs in to the Backend directly is recorded as themselves.

Actions taken through the Portal, such as break-glass validations and notes on a Case, are recorded under the Operator who took them, as before. This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.
The findings listed under each proposed project read as plain sentences, with amounts and periods written out. This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.

Role grants and changes to an excluded group keep the IP address the change was made from, as policy changes already did. About 20 minutes after a change, the Backend looks up the city and country and the affected account's details once, and stores them with the case.
The city, country and last sign-in require Entra ID P1 in the customer's tenant, and the case explains when they are missing. The update needs no new app permissions.
Sign-ins listed on a case show the full country name, such as "Norway" instead of "NO". This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.
Guidance on how to fix a finding writes a path through a Microsoft portal with ">" between its steps, for example "App registrations > Authentication".
Headlines for privileged role grants read, for example, "Tier 0 role: Global Administrator". Extra roles in the privileged access list are written "(Permanent, Direct)".
No check was added or removed, and no severity changed. This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.
Finding descriptions and recommendations, Alert and Case text, invitation emails and error messages are rewritten in plain wording. No check was added or removed, and no severity changed.
Citations now read, for example, "supports Art. 21(2)(i): access control". The Azure check for Defender for Cloud plans is renamed to "No paid Defender for Cloud plan is enabled on any subscription".
Existing Alerts and Cases keep their original text. Findings show the new wording after the next scan.
